correctness.rationale: For \(d\ge2n\) an exact eigenvalue reduction gives \(T=(\lambda_{\max}(G)-n/d)^2/n\). Joint Gaussian-coordinate and independent biased-sign product central limit theorems produce the zero-diagonal W matrix and its \(a(J-I)\) deformation; the latter uses a directly computed covariance and bounded Lindeberg terms. Eigenvalue continuity and null quantile continuity yield exact-calibrated local power; an all-ones Rayleigh quotient gives power one when \(\sqrt d\,\mu_d^2\) diverges. For \(n=2\), an exact Beta Haar inner-product law and exact Binomial cube-product count yield finite-dimensional critical values and power, agreeing with a shifted folded-normal limit. The standalone checker passed 751 reproducibility assertions, but finite checks are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: For a published spherical-uniformity test, the theorem identifies a sharp dimension-dependent bias threshold and a nontrivial entire local power curve. Even an exactly singular alternative at zero bias is undetected asymptotically; the exact two-observation Beta/Binomial formula and evaluated critical values make the calibration consequence independently reproducible. The result delineates an operational boundary of the operator-norm statistic rather than an arbitrary numerical invariant.
